filesize._comment: Two different reasons, kept apart on purpose. addon/BabelChat/img/ holds binary assets: the gate counts newline bytes, so a 128x128 TGA registers as 958 'lines' of nothing. The named files are vendored third-party libraries — LibBabble ships one generated table per locale and is not ours to split; naming them individually rather than exempting Libs/ wholesale keeps the cap on any first-party Lua that lands in that tree.
filesize._comment_i18n: app/i18n.py is a string table — 166 keys x 3 languages and about thirty lines of mechanism. Splitting the data into app/locales/<lang>.py is the actual fix and is tracked as its own task; exempting it here keeps the cap meaningful for the modules where line count still measures complexity, instead of inviting the table to be chopped in half at an arbitrary key.
